args.title: payments-api elevated error rate after v5.1.0 deploy
args.summary: payments-api is unhealthy in production following this morning's deploy to v5.1.0. All three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are on v5.1.0 with an error rate of ~18%. Release history shows v5.0.0 was healthy and v5.1.0 as the first degraded release. Action taken: rolled back payments-api to v5.0.0 in all production regions. Further investigation needed into the v5.1.0 regression before any redeploy.

trace.final:
Done. Both actions completed and verified.

**Rollback**
- The affected service is named **`payments-api`** (not `payments`). It was unhealthy at 18% error rate, with all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v5.1.0.
- Release history: v5.0.0 → healthy, v5.1.0 → degraded. So **v5.0.0 was the most recent release healthy in production**.
- Rolled back all production regions to **v5.0.0**. Verified: `healthy: true`, error rate down from 18% to **0.2%**.
- Policy note: the destination version (v5.0.0) was previously healthy in production, so this was a standard rollback and did not require change-manager approval.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, on `payments-api`, titled "payments-api elevated error rate after v5.1.0 deploy", with a summary covering the symptoms, release history, rollback action, and the need to investigate the v5.1.0 regression before any redeploy. On-call was paged.

**Suggested follow-up:** v5.1.0 is still the candidate for a fix — note that redeploying it (or any version never healthy in production) will require change-manager approval under the org policy, so it should be scoped as a change-managed deploy once root-caused, not a quick re-roll.

One caveat worth flagging: I inferred the service name by probing conventions after `payments` was rejected. `payments-api` matched the described symptoms (errors since this morning's deploy) exactly, but if your org has other payment-related services, it's worth confirming this was the one your users reported.
